items.title: Sudan: Drought and war push Darfur and Kordofan towards famine
items.summary: The risk of famine is growing in parts of Sudan already torn apart by war, as a severe El Niño drought makes life even harder in Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan, the UN-backed global hunger monitor warned on Monday.

items.title: Myanmar Military Steps Up Airstrikes in Rakhine as Ground Offensive Stalls
items.summary: Crisis Group expert Thomas Kean examines why the Myanmar military’s faltering counteroffensive and escalating air attacks have further dimmed prospects for a ceasefire in Rakhine State.

items.title: Security Council LIVE: Syria’s fragile transition – economic strain, Israeli incursions and progress towards elections
items.summary: The Security Council met to debate Syria's thorny transition Monday as it faces pressure on several fronts. Economic hardship is fuelling unrest, Israeli incursions continue in the south and sectarian tensions persist in Sweida, even as Damascus reports progress on its chemical weapons programme and talks about future elections. Millions, meanwhile, remain displaced. Follow live below and go here for full meetings coverage.

items.title: ‘Efficiency has limits’: UNHCR chief warns refugee protection is buckling under cuts
items.summary: The money is running out faster than needs are growing: with 117 million men, women and children now forced from their homes, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received just $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year – and its chief, Barham Salih, warns that the global support system for asylum-seekers risks buckling.

items.title: Centcom Forces Disable Cargo Vessel Attempting to Violate Blockade
items.summary: Service members operating in the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility recently disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman, after the ship's crew ignored repeated warnings and attempted to run the ongoing naval blockade against Iran.

items.title: Yemen: WFP warns of potential ‘humanitarian catastrophe’ as fighting blocks aid delivery
items.summary: Intensifying fighting in Yemen has cut off life-saving assistance to 800,000 people as shifting frontlines, blocked roads and growing insecurity severely restrict access to the city of Taiz and other conflict zones, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) said on Wednesday.

items.summary: The Saudi energy ministry says the Houthi attack caused a "limited fire" at Aramco's headquarters complex in Dhahran.

items.title: Security Council, 10241st Meeting (AM) Haiti
items.summary: The Security Council will vote on a draft resolution to extend the sanctions regime on Haiti. The regime, which was established in 2022 and includes a travel ban, asset freeze and arms embargo, was last renewed on 17 October 2025 with the adoption of resolution 2794 (2025).

items.title: Toward a Thaw in the Cambodia-Thailand Border Conflict
items.summary: Hostilities between Cambodia and Thailand ceased in late 2025, after two rounds of combat along the frontier. But the truce is under growing strain. To avoid more war, the two countries should restore normal diplomatic ties and resume work on demarcating their shared border.

items.title: ‘Need for UN has never been greater,’ UN chief says, proposing slimmer $3.3 billion budget for 2027
items.summary: Amid climate disruption, an AI revolution, war and growing hunger, “the need for the United Nations has never been greater,” Secretary-General António Guterres said on Tuesday, presenting a $3.3 billion programme budget proposal for next year – a cut of $40.8 million.

items.title: Niger Wrestles with the Aftermath of a Military Revolt
items.summary: A mutiny by Niger’s special forces in late August morphed into a coup attempt. In this Q&A, Crisis Group experts explain how the unrest exposed growing discontent within the military’s ranks.

items.title: 800 million young people face a future without jobs
items.summary: Approximately 800 million young people entering the labour market in developing economies over the coming years will not find jobs unless countries act, the head of the UN Development Programme (UNDP) warned on Tuesday, as the agency launched two initiatives to boost investment and employment.

items.title: Colombia peace deal must endure as insecurity grows, Security Council hears
items.summary: Nearly 10 years after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement to end a decades-long insurgency, the deal is under strain from growing insecurity – and the UN’s top official in the country says it cannot be allowed to falter.
